Earlier I had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee

function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with a given portion size to track dietary intake. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log, such as 'apple', 'bread', or 'chicken breast'.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, specified in the unit given by portion_unit. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount, such as 'cup', 'grams', or 'slice'.

meal_type.description: The type of meal or snack this food item is being logged for.

log_date.description: The date and time when the food was consumed, in ISO 8601 format such as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

message.reasoning: We need to log foods. The user says they had 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea. Also earlier had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee. We should log each item. For each log, we need to call the function log_food. We can log multiple calls. The function signature: food_name, portion_amount, portion_unit, meal_type optional, log_date optional. We don't have dates; we can omit log_date. Meal_type default is snack. But maybe we can specify meal_type if known. They didn't specify meal times. So we can just use default snack. We'll log four items: frozen mango (8 pieces), chai tea (maybe 1 cup?), pepperoni pizza (2 slices), coffee (1 cup). But the user didn't specify units. We can guess: pieces for mango, slice for pizza, cup for tea and coffee. Use portion_unit accordingly. Let's do separate calls.
